title: Some Reformed who subscribe Dort take the same way, notably Robert Baron of Aberdeen, who follows Fonseca
source_text: III. Sed inter eos etiam Reformatos qui alioqui videntur ab Arminiano dogmate alieni, & Dordracenae Synodo subscribunt, reperiuntur nonnulli qui hanc quoque viam sequuntur, ut Providentiae Divinae decreta cum arbitrii humani libertate concilient. Quo de numero est Robertus Baronius Abredoniae in Scotia ante aliquot annos Theologiae Professor. Is enim in Metaphysica ad Theologiae usum accommodata Fonsecae doctrinam hac in parte laudat, eique aperte subscribit. Sect. 12. disput. 2. num. 65.
pass_a_gloss: III. But among those Reformed also who otherwise seem alien from the Arminian dogma, and subscribe the Synod of Dort, some are found who also follow this way, that they may reconcile the decrees of Divine Providence with the freedom of human choice. Of which number is Robert Baron, some years ago Professor of Theology at Aberdeen in Scotland. For he in the Metaphysics accommodated to the use of Theology praises the doctrine of Fonseca in this part, and openly subscribes to it. Sect. 12. disput. 2. num. 65.
pass_b_english: Yet even among the Reformed who otherwise seem far from the Arminian teaching and subscribe to the Synod of Dort, some follow this same way of reconciling the decrees of God's providence with the freedom of human choice.

One of them is Robert Baron, some years ago professor of theology at Aberdeen in Scotland. In his Metaphysics adapted to the use of theology he praises Fonseca's teaching on this point and openly endorses it: section 12, disputation 2, number 65.
